name: Scapegoat
overview: The Scriptures in Leviticus 16 reveal the institution of the scapegoat as part of the Day of Atonement ritual, where two goats are presented before the LORD and lots are cast to designate one for the LORD and the other as the scapegoat (Leviticus 16:7-8). The goat chosen for the LORD is offered as a sin offering (Leviticus 16:9), while the scapegoat is presented alive to bear the iniquities and transgressions of Israel, symbolically carrying their sins away into the wilderness (Leviticus 16:10, 16:20-21). This act of confession and sending away the scapegoat underscores the seriousness of sin and the need for atonement through substitution, pointing believers to the ultimate fulfillment in Christ's atoning work.
